findings: ETT.tex:1713-1724, in the readings DEC-25, OQ-18, OQ-34/OQ-35 and OQ-82: the remark holds at every Hausdorff E_{>=0}-manifold with a BTZ point, for every absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point, the natural one included (Causal.SingularRowsGeroch.mesure_unilaterale, mesure_unilaterale_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25), with no hypothesis left, mixed manifolds included. The paper's computation is the proof: J^-(q) \ J^-(p) is the segment ]p,q] of the BTZ line through q (Jminus_diff_eq_segment, from SFALine.Jminus_eq_image), every point of it is BTZ with empty chronological past, and it lies in J^+(p) \ K^+(p) since K^+(p) = I^+(p) (segment_subset); property 3. in the past and property 4. in the future then conflict (not_admissible_both_of_le). It does not go through SingularFlatAxioms and needs no second countability.

ETT.tex:1716, « Let M be a causal E_{>=0}-manifold »: the conclusion does not need « causal ». Any causality carrying a measure admissible in the past (or in the future) is causal: for p <= q <= p with p != q, property 3. asks mu(J^-(q) \ J^-(p)) > 0, and that set is empty (Causal.SingularRowsGeroch.isCausal_of_admissiblePast, isCausal_of_admissibleFuture; model-free). So the remark holds at every Hausdorff E_{>=0}-manifold with a BTZ point, causal or not. The paper's computation does use causality (the segment), so the author may keep the word. The same fact says that defi:mesure_dieckmann (l.1034-1043) forces causality on any topological spacetime that carries an admissible measure. It is consistent with the existing finding behind DEC-18 (E_alpha modulo a translation carries no measure admissible in the past).

Sharpness, both ways. At a strongly causal, Hausdorff, second countable E_{>=0}-manifold with a BTZ point, each one-sided notion is inhabited and no measure has both (mesure_unilaterale_sharp, with SFAManifolds.mesure_admissible). The BTZ point cannot be dropped: E_pi has no BTZ point and carries one measure admissible in the past and in the future at once (epi_admissible_both, MeasuresEAlpha.exists_admissible_past_future).

Witnesses, each conclusion out of this file's M-level theorems (not E0.mesure_unilaterale): E_0 (nonvacuous_e0_unilaterale: hmin, IsoChartsCoverDEC25, strong causality, sing_0 nonempty, the two one-sided measures, none both; nonvacuous_e0_natural: the natural-causality form).

sorries.obstruction: (iii)=>(i) at a strongly causal, connected, Hausdorff, second countable E_{>=0}-manifold. The paper's route is theo:geroch's cited (iii)=>(i) (O'Neill, Prop. 8 and Thm 35), which is false for topological spacetimes as formalized (OQ-32, chronological Minkowski space). findings: ETT.tex:1771-1785, the proved directions, in the readings DEC-25, OQ-18, OQ-34/OQ-35, OQ-82 and DEC-15. (i)=>(ii) and (i)=>(iii) hold at every Hausdorff, second countable E_{>=0}-manifold, for every absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point, the natural one included (Causal.SingularRowsGeroch.geroch_sing_i_imp_ii, geroch_sing_i_imp_iii, and their _of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25 forms). They need neither connectedness nor strong causality, and no hypothesis is left: SingularFlatAxioms, ModelMeasures and strong causality are proved. (ii)=>(iii) holds at every strongly causal one (geroch_sing_ii_imp_iii). The proof's « direct consequence of Theorem theo:geroch and of Proposition prop:mesure_admissible » (l.1781-1785) is sound for these three directions. Witnesses, each out of the M-level theorems: E_0 (nonvacuous_e0_geroch, nonvacuous_e0_natural) and E_pi, a massive line (nonvacuous_epi_geroch).

ETT.tex:1771-1779, the equivalence, stated at genuine E_{>=0}-manifolds, connected and strongly causal (DEC-18): Causal.SingularRowsGeroch.geroch_sing and geroch_sing_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25. They rest only on geroch_sing_iii_imp_i, this file's one sorry. OQ-33's counterexample to the abstract form (CausalScaffold.SingularGeroch.geroch_sing_of_stronglyCausal) does not reach this statement. Chronological Minkowski space has an isomorphic chart at no point, for any singular structure. Argued by hand: a chart isomorphism carries ≤ and ≪ of an open set onto a model's, every open set of a model contains a pair x ≤ y, x ≠ y, not x ≪ y, and the reflexive chronological causality excludes such pairs. It is not formalized, because chronoMinkowski lives in the scaffold module CausalScaffold.GerochCauchy, which has a sorry. So the paper's theorem, read at E_{>=0}-manifolds, is not refuted. OQ-33's question (should SingularFlatAxioms carry the local closedness) then bears on a proof route through the abstraction, not on the statement. What remains is OQ-32's repair of (iii)=>(i), with the local closedness that genuine E_{>=0}-manifolds have.

ETT.tex:1778, « Moreover »: at every connected, causal, Hausdorff, second countable E_{>=0}-manifold the splitting holds given the flow of lem:vecteur (geroch_sing_split, through Causality.SingularFlatAxioms.geroch_sing_split). The structure is not used by that proof, and VecteurFlow stays a named hypothesis. lem:vecteur's X is parallel to the BTZ lines at BTZ points (l.1756), so its orbit through a BTZ point is null. The library's chronal-flow route to the splitting (Causal.Splitting, HasChronalCausalFlow.nonempty_isCauchySplitting) therefore does not apply at a BTZ line. Only its causal-flow form, which asks J^±(S) closed, could (IsCausalFlow.exists_isCauchySplitting). Not pursued.
